title: Sanitized ProvisioningAction request and response journaling

outcomes.statement: Every connector call persists a canonical sanitized request and response summary that provably excludes credentials, authorization headers, raw PII, full provider identifiers and raw provider bodies.
outcomes.demo: A call writes a ProvisioningAction row whose summary survives a property-based check asserting no forbidden token appears for any generated payload.

uncertainties.statement: No live Anthropic credentials exist; the live provider probe is blocked on per-org keys and invite-canary authorization.
uncertainties.resolution: Scope is deterministic fixtures backed by passing Pact consumer contracts. Live credential-scope, organization-binding, pagination, rate-limit and invite acceptance stay gated behind the authorized provider run named in the parent story's AC4, and must not be claimed here.

uncertainties.statement: Probe code under scripts/probes/** cannot be imported by the connector, because that path is exempted from the provider-boundary lint for the probe's benefit only.
uncertainties.resolution: Semantics are ported into packages/connectors/src/providers/anthropic/, the other exempt path, and re-implemented against the connector's own contracts so core code keeps importing only the vendor-neutral interface.

uncertainties.statement: This work needs the transport seam, which US-056 delivers, but a blocked_by dependency is unconditionally blocking in this validator and would permanently prevent a ready decision.
uncertainties.resolution: The edge is recorded as a blocks dependency on US-056 instead. Execution is sequenced after US-056 lands; no separate readiness state is required because the seam exists before this starts.

uncertainties.statement: An allow-list and a deny-list sanitizer fail differently on unexpected provider fields.
uncertainties.resolution: Canonical summaries are built from an explicit allow-list, so an unknown provider field is dropped rather than leaked. That is the fail-closed direction and is asserted directly.
